case: MySQL/MariaDB typed CSV and SQL-file round trips preserve empty VARCHAR under MariaDB EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL
engine: MariaDB 11 and MySQL Docker integration fixtures

behavior_before_fix.result: The MariaDB SQL-file copy matched all 7 source rows, but typed CSV restore matched only 6 of 7 under EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL; the empty VARCHAR was converted to SQL NULL.
behavior_before_fix.test_delta: The VARCHAR column, empty value and native byte/NULL checks were added before the baseline run; the core import planner was unchanged.

fix: MySQL CSV planning now recognizes empty values for ENUM/SET and CHAR/VARCHAR/TEXT destination types and expands them as CASE WHEN marker = 1 THEN SPACE(0) ELSE value END. Explicit marker-bound SQL NULL remains NULL. The MySQL SQL-file literal writer already emits SPACE(0) for empty text values.
contract: The native source includes ordinary empty VARCHAR, nonempty text, and SQL NULL alongside enum/set boundary values.
Typed CSV restore and replayed SQL files are compared independently against native ENUM ordinals and bytes, SET masks and bytes, VARCHAR bytes, NULL state, and an untouched sibling.
MariaDB runs EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL alone and combined with STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, ANSI_QUOTES, and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, in addition to the established mode matrix.
MySQL continues to pass the established twelve-mode consumer matrix.
Core planner tests pin emitted SQL and restrict the empty-string workaround to enum/set and text-family destinations.
